title: Evaluation of feasibility and technical success of MR-assisted percutaneous sclerotherapy of slow-flow vascular malformations avoiding ionizing radiation.
summary:
Slow-flow vascular malformations, which are classified into venous malformations (VMs) and lymphatic malformations (LMs) as well as mixed forms, are a congenital condition that primarily affects children and young adults . The dysplastic lesions, which often cause pain, aesthetic impairment, functional deficits or, in the case of lymphatic malformations, recurrent infections, are treated by percutaneous sclerotherapy as the treatment of choice. The standard treatment procedure consists of two parts. First, the target structure is identified and visualized by ultrasound and one or more guide needles are inserted into the lesion. Additional iodinated contrast material is injected under X-ray fluoroscopy to identify both flow within the lesion and characteristics of any draining veins. This is followed by administration of the sclerosant under x-ray fluoroscopy. However, certain malformations cannot be detected by ultrasound. Typically, these are lesions that are located far from the skin surface, are within or behind osseous structures, or have been previously treated with consecutive fibrosis and scarring. In addition, most vascular malformations require multiple therapy sessions that repeatedly expose patients (often children and young adults) and clinical staff to ionizing radiation.
Magnetic resonance (MR)-guided sclerotherapy has the potential to be a safer alternative to the aforementioned modalities, as it eliminates radiation exposure and allows better visualization of target lesions as well as surrounding soft tissues and critical structures, even in deep tissue layers.  Especially for lesions that cannot be reached by conservative treatment techniques described above, MR-guided sclerotherapy is a promising alternative.
conditions: Other specified congenital malformation syndromes affecting multiple systems

interventions.name: All patients included in this study have the indication for image-guided minimally invasive intervention independent of this study. The indication is based on the relevant guidelines or on the decision of the interdisciplinary discussions between interventional radiologists, angiologists, pediatric

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Clinical indication for percutaneous sclerotherapy of slow-flow vascular malformation (venous/lymphatic/combined malformation). The indication for intervention in this case must be independent of the presented study.
- The localization of the vascular malformation is not or not sufficiently accessible by conventional imaging (sonography and X-ray fluoroscopy).
- Previous therapy (surgery, embolization, sclerotherapy) without improvement of symptoms.
- Platelets > 50,000/mm3 (50 GPt/l)
- INR/PTT <1.5 times upper normal value (patients taking anticoagulants may be included if no underlying coagulation abnormality has been previously identified).
- Signed informed consent form
- Age: children and adults >4 years
Exclusion criteria:
- Lack of informed consent and/or lack of capacity to consent to the study. 
- Contraindications to MRI examination, especially implants not suitable for MR, tattoos or piercings, limiting claustrophobia.
- Contraindications to contrast agents (only in the case of MR contrast agent use):
o Known allergy to MR contrast media.
o Higher grade renal insufficiency (GFR <30 ml/min).
- Contraindications to image-guided interstitial intervention.
o Platelets < 50,000/mm3 (50 GPt/l)
o INR/PTT> 1.5 -fold upper normal value
o Presence of an abnormality of blood coagulation.
- Patients with high-flow vascular malformations or other vascular abnormalities (vascular tumors).
- Concomitant consumptive disease or ECOG > 1.
- Contraindications for invasive treatments
